answer: In an economy of AI agents, Sybil resistance can be enforced through a cryptographic proof-of-work mechanism requiring nodes to expend computational energy, much like mining rare copper resources from a vast digital ocean. By anchoring agent identities to staked tokens or verifiable GPU compute tied to a physical ridge of specialized hardware, the system imposes a prohibitive financial and energetic cost. An attacker attempting to flood the network with fake identities faces exponential scaling costs, making mass fabrication economically non-viable.
